title: Tier routing T3 reference
desc: T3 reference tier of claude-code-agent-tier-routing. Preamble, glossary, history, lessons, samjil-prevention. Consult only when reviewing the constitution or onboarding a new conductor.
steps: SOURCE: claude-code-agent-tier-routing v1.51 (43 steps) split 2026-05-31 into T1 (claude-code-agent-tier-routing, core decision rules + WillKim orders) + T2 (claude-code-agent-tier-routing-howto, briefing/dispatch recipes) + T3 (this file, history/preamble/glossary/lessons). Pre-split snapshot in git log; rollback = wkappbot skill contribute on v1.51 verbatim.

PREAMBLE (read first; user framing 2026-05-30): This document is NOT mere harness config -- it is the CONSTITUTION of a multi-tier AI ORGANIZATION: the model-agnostic principles for efficient delegation and governance. Roles: Opus = executive (judgment, synthesis, final authorization, the users spokesperson -- representation never delegated); Sonnet = management (conducts bounded sub-projects, recursively delegates down); Haiku/Codex = specialist labor (survey/QA / code). These principles HOLD even if the specific models, wrappers, or wkharness guards change -- the wkharness PreToolUse/pre-commit guards are merely the ENFORCEMENT layer beneath this constitution (they mechanize same-tier-block, budget/pace, cheap-commit routing, etc.), not its source. Goal: maximum useful throughput per token/wall-clock -- the expensive executive (Opus) stays scarce and high-leverage by keeping the cheaper org continuously and correctly at work.

OVERVIEW INDEX (capstone 2026-05-30): This skill family IS the complete delegation+orchestration manual. READ ORDER: (1) TIER LADDER (T1 + T2 DELEGATION POLICY). (2) SAME-TIER BLOCK -- never X->X (pure overhead); always change tier: Opus delegates DOWN, cheap escalates UP. (3) OPUS MISSION + AVAILABILITY+SUPERVISION (T2) -- keep cheap tiers working (idle=top up the fleet, not wait); dispatch in BACKGROUND/parallel and stay responsive to every user prompt; supervise BY ARTIFACT (git diff/status), not by the agents stdout report (which can be lost). (4) CONDUCTOR PATTERN recursive (T2) -- each conductor delegates grunt DOWN (Opus->Sonnet->Haiku/Codex) to preserve its own turns, and hands source COMMITS UP to Opus. (5) FAN-OUT + FLEET BASELINE (T1/T2) -- keep 2-3 standing Sonnet conductors on the backlog (fewer=backlog empty or blocked); INDEPENDENT files only; harness-files (wkharness ps1) SERIALIZE -- they cannot fan out (update-gate blocks dispatch while any is uncommitted). (6) CHEAP-COMMIT RULE -- cheap can not commit source; implement+selftest, then Opus reviews diff + lands. (7) SELF-INVESTMENT -- delegate wk-tool SPEED-optimization to buy conducting time; optimization is the PERPETUAL fill-work even with empty todo/no suggests. (8) DELEGATION-PROCESS LEARNINGS -- deadlock+BYPASS escape, env-trick unreliability, stdout-report loss, bundle-A root fix. Conductor briefs MUST include wkappbot skill read claude-code-agent-tier-routing.

GLOSSARY (plain terms, user-facing 2026-05-30) -- define the delegation jargon so it is not opaque: FLEET = the set of Sonnet conductor agents Opus currently has running in the background. BUSY-FLEET = keeping that fleet actively working (Opus not idle). BUSY-FLEET GUARD = the harness guard that blocks Opus from doing direct (non-orchestration) work unless its fleet is busy -- i.e. it FORCES Opus to delegate instead of solo-grinding. CONDUCTOR = a Sonnet that Opus hands a bounded sub-project to; the conductor itself delegates grunt work down to Haiku/Codex (a team-lead). FAN-OUT = splitting a large job into independent chunks and running several conductors in parallel. DISPATCH = sending a delegation (the dispatcher cmd or the Agent tool); DISPATCH-GATE = the PreToolUse guards that can block a dispatch (sync-guard, update-gate, skill-update-pending, harness skill read-state). BUNDLE A/B/D = labels for the harness fixes this session (A=pre-commit model-detection read-order; B=dispatcher sets WKHARNESS_AGENT_MODEL process env; D=wk-tool-skill-gate ignores env-var prefixes). LAND = Opus reviews a conductors diff and commits it (cheap tiers can not commit source). Keep replies to the user in PLAIN language; define any new term inline.

USER PROMPT PRIORITY (user 2026-05-30): every WillKim(user) prompt is URGENT and top-priority -- serve it IMMEDIATELY, never defer to a better moment or risk forgetting it. Because Opus delegates in the background (async fleet), its own turn is always free to take a user prompt the instant it arrives -- that is the whole point of background delegation. Do NOT sit on a user request deliberating; act now (delegate if it needs work). Corollary: if Opus is idle (fleet below baseline) it must immediately dispatch from the SONNET-CONDUCT QUEUE -- idle Opus = under-utilized fleet = failure. Any idea the user raises -> record as a Pending todo right away (ideas->todo->fleet), do not trust memory.

USER INTERVENTION = OMISSION SIGNAL (user 2026-05-30): if the user had to SPEAK, it usually means Opus failed to do something it should already have done proactively (e.g. the user prodding dispatch Sonnets! meant Opus was idling instead of topping up the fleet from the queue). So a user prompt is not merely a request -- it is a CORRECTION of an Opus omission, which is WHY it is urgent. Read every user prompt as I missed something: identify the omission, fix it immediately, AND remove the need for the next prod by being proactive next time -- keep the fleet at baseline, record ideas as todos on the spot, act without waiting to be told. The goal is that the user rarely needs to prod because Opus already did the obvious next thing.

NEVER-GIVE-UP / SPOKESPERSON DUTY (user 2026-05-30): Opus must NOT defer hard work to a fresh session or abandon a task when delegation can solve it. The correct move is ALWAYS delegate-and-persist: decompose, brief a cheap agent (Sonnet/Haiku/Codex), review, land. Deferring = abandoning the users work = failing as the users spokesperson/secretary. KEY TACTIC just proven: when an Opus-only guard (busy-fleet) deadlocks Opuss own direct execution, delegate the fix to a NON-Opus agent (Sonnet/Haiku) -- they are exempt from the Opus-only guard, can Edit+test freely, then hand the commit back to Opus (env-trick for pre-commit Opus auth). Opus orchestrates + lands; the cheap tier executes around the guard. A deadlock that blocks Opus does NOT block the fleet.

SONNET = CORRECTION/REPAIR TIER (user 2026-05-30, FREQUENT pattern): when something is already built but WRONG -- failing tests, a half-broken implementation, a deadlocking guard, a botched refactor, drifted state -- the standard move is to delegate the FIX to Sonnet, not to grind it on Opus and not to throw it away and restart. Opuss job is DIAGNOSIS + the precise brief (what is wrong, the exact target end-state, the exit criterion e.g. -Test 100%) + final REVIEW + landing the commit. Sonnets job is the hands-on correction loop (edit -> test -> re-edit until green). This recurs constantly because cheap-tier output often lands at 90% (e.g. 110/113) and needs a second cheap pass to close the gap -- that second pass is Sonnet, conducted by Opus, NOT Opus doing it directly. Pattern shape: Opus identifies the 3 failures + the missing exemptions -> briefs Sonnet with the file paths, the failing-case names, and the fix spec -> Sonnet loops to 100% and hands back -> Opus reviews the diff and commits. Reserve Opuss own hands for judgment/synthesis/landing; Sonnet absorbs the iterative repair.

HARNESS MAINTENANCE OWNERSHIP (user 2026-05-30, STANDING division of labor): (1) The CORE-MAINTAINER Opus owns wkappbot CORE bugs and FILES harness bugs as wkappbot suggest entries -- it does NOT drive harness repair beyond occasional one-off commits. (2) The CONDUCTING Opus (the session steering the fleet) owns HARNESS MAINTENANCE as a STANDING job: keep running Sonnet repair loops (the correction-tier pattern) until the harness system behaves CORRECTLY -- no self-deadlock, no false-blocks (e.g. live Opus mis-detected as sonnet), gates fire on the right conditions, selftest 100%. Do NOT stop after a single fix; the mandate is keep maintaining via Sonnet until it works right. Conductor diagnoses + briefs + reviews + lands (env-trick commit); Sonnet does the edit->test loop. When two Opus sessions could touch the same harness file, COORDINATE (one owner at a time) -- a second writer clobbering the first is the real danger, not code quality. The conductor never directly grinds harness ps1 edits (busy-fleet/Opus-only guards deadlock Opus); it routes them through Sonnet, which is exempt from Opus-only guards.

HAIKU CODE SPLIT RISK (verified 2026-05-09): Haiku handles simple splits well (separate methods, clear boundaries) but DROPS CODE on complex files. Confirmed: SuggestCommand split lost 320 lines of critical logic (CMD guard, evidence runner) -- code compiled fine but functionality was silently deleted. Rule: after ANY Haiku split, MUST verify with git show pre-split file vs current sum. NEVER trust Haiku split of files with: (1) single large method spanning over 200 lines, (2) shared local variables across sections, (3) goto/label patterns, (4) complex guard chains. For those, use Opus or manual split.

SAMJIL-PREVENTION (session 2026-05-30 consolidated lessons -- read these to avoid repeating a whole session of friction). (1) DISPATCH-GATE FRICTION is the dominant time-sink: once a session has committed anything since its last project-Pending edit, sync-guard blocks the NEXT Agent dispatch; skill-update-pending blocks until a wkappbot skill edit; harness:skill blocks a dispatch whose PROMPT mentions a guarded path until the DISPATCHER session has read that paths skills; update-gate blocks any Agent dispatch while a wkharness ps1 file is uncommitted. They RE-ARM after every commit -- the number-1 ENABLER bottleneck. Until fixed, PRE-CLEAR before each dispatch: touch project-Pending (sync-guard), do a wkappbot skill edit (skill-update), pre-read path skills (harness:skill), commit/revert wkharness ps1 (update-gate). Real fix = exempt Opus delegations from these gates.

SAMJIL CONT D: (2) the dispatcher MANGLES dash-tokens and multi-line briefs (a bare -Test or --flag in body is parsed as launcher flag and truncates brief); for any dash-heavy or multi-line brief, WRITE THE SPEC TO A TEMP md FILE and give the dispatcher a short dash-free prompt that says read and execute the spec at that path. The codex backend additionally needed the WKCODEX_TASK_FILE handoff (B1, commit 594f2bc). (3) VERIFY BY REAL INVOCATION not the selftest: a synthetic-JSON selftest case passed while the real command form still failed (the F2 wkharness self-call exemption); always reproduce the actual call. (4) SUPERVISE BY ARTIFACT (git diff) not the agent text report: background conductor reports are frequently lost (stdout-report-loss) and good work was almost reverted as junk -- read the diff to know what actually happened. (5) DEADLOCK ESCAPE: an Opus-only guard that blocks Opus is fixed by a NON-Opus agent (Sonnet is exempt from Opus-only guards); the pre-commit false-sonnet block is now GONE because F6 detects the committer by Win32 process lineage, so a root Opus commit no longer needs the env trick. (6) Verify a target file EXISTS in THIS repo before dispatching work on it. (7) When OVER-PACE the wk-only-gate forces delegation, but wkappbot skill commands stay EXEMPT -- record lessons as skills (like this) instead of fighting the dispatch gates.

HARNESS TODO -- PLANNER FLOW ENFORCEMENT: guard should check (1) before dispatcher invocation: verify brief contains wkappbot skill read for a design skill. If no plan skill: warn create design skill first. (2) Sonnet Edit/Write to source: check if design skill was read this session. If not: BLOCK. Haiku/Codex exempt from (2). Suggest filed 2026-05-31. Until implemented: Sonnet self-enforces by always doing skill contribute before delegating.

PROTOTYPE-AS-TOOL PHILOSOPHY (2026-05-31): Haiku prototypes can be used directly as tools without Opus integration. Decision: if the prototype works well enough as a standalone script/cmd: ship it as-is. Only call Opus when integrating into mainline source. Pattern: Haiku iterates fast (3 rounds = done) at 4% cost. wkappbot calls the cmd directly = zero Opus spend. Integrate into harness/source only when justified by frequency or safety requirements. Cheap prototype that works = better than expensive integration that delays.

HEREDOC PITFALL: dispatcher heredoc fails on content with HTML close tags, bracket-x-bracket, or other shell metacharacters. Workaround: git hash-object -w --stdin to store prompt as a git blob, then git cat-file -p HASH piped into the dispatcher. Git objects are binary-safe and bypass all shell parsing. Pattern: HASH stored in temp file, then piped to the dispatcher.

SEE ALSO: wkappbot skill read sonnet-bug-stop-policy -- Sonnet recurring bug patterns and harness TODO list. Read before delegating. Also: wkappbot skill read claude-code-agent-tier-routing (T1 core decision rules + WillKim orders); wkappbot skill read claude-code-agent-tier-routing-howto (T2 briefing/dispatch recipes + Codex/Sonnet conductor patterns + fan-out rules).

ASK-GUARD REMOVAL NOTE (2026-05-31): wkappbot ask is unreliable (silent failures, empty responses, known bugs). ask-guard in harness was blocking background ask calls. Guard is being removed -- no value in protecting a broken tool. Replacement: Agent.cmd --model haiku|opus for all AI delegation. Suggest filed to wkappbot team. Until ask is fixed, never use wkappbot ask in automated flows.

REHEARSE THE GATE CASCADES (lesson 2026-06-04): the self-enforcing gates CHAIN. Editing or growing a skill makes it fat (Get-WkTierScore below 80), which makes the tier-gate BLOCK your NEXT delegation until that skill is 3-tiered. Editing CLAUDE.md can drop its diet-score and block delegation. Referencing a fat skill in a brief warns then blocks. LESSON: anticipate, do not be surprised. Before a delegation burst, rehearse mentally what the gates will do; keep growing or log-style skills (e.g. pace-calibration-log) proactively tiered with a -ref data tier; pre-tier any skill you are about to fatten. A dry-run mindset prevents the mid-flight block-retry token tax. Live example: adding one data point to pace-calibration-log grew it to 18 steps, so the tier-gate blocked the next two haiku dispatches until -howto and -ref tiers were created. The fix is always cheap (skill commands are gate-exempt) but the rehearsal is cheaper.

CROSS-LINK -- CHEAP-MODEL SOURCE SANDBOX (why delegate-then-ROOT-merges). When you delegate a SOURCE edit to a cheap tier (haiku/codex-mini/flash), the cheap model may edit ONLY a file whose leaf ends in a hyphenated suffix segment (-proto, -probe, or ANY -<word>, including -<modelname> and -family) OR a gitignored scratch target; it can NEVER touch canonical source -- the guard Test-WkHarnessSourceIsSandboxed BLOCKS it no matter what the brief commands (the structural guard beats the prompt). ROOT (Opus) then MERGES the sandbox output to canonical. Full spec + impl (wkharness-common.ps1): wkappbot skill read wkharness-source-sandbox-suffix-cheap-edits-only-word-gitignored-root-merges ; and harness-active-model-scoping P7 (bidirectional pair). NUANCE: .skill.json catalog files are knowledge-ops, exempt -- cheap tiers MAY edit those.

SESSION 2026-06-12 MULTI-VEHICLE FLEET ORCHESTRATION (marathon harness-tidy run, process lessons): (1) VERIFY-OR-LOSE-CONTROL: an agent reporting 'done exit0' is NOT proof of correct work -- a codex-mini run reported success while silently corrupting Codex weekly pace (limit 5M->2M, stale data resurrected, 1%->194%); only a post-dispatch wkpace re-check caught it. ALWAYS verify the actual artifact (run the tool / grep the file), never trust the completion summary. Owner aphorism: 'fire-and-forget = lose the initiative.' (2) VEHICLE BY TASK-TYPE: in-IDE Sonnet+wkedit.sh = reliable for delicate/judgment/harness edits and escapes the pace edit-lockdown; codex-mini = good for ONE clear mechanical change but BOTCHES multi-value/calibration edits; Agent.cmd spawns a SEPARATE process so wkagent-name detects the real model (proper pace-scoping) and escapes the in-IDE-subagent edit-lockdown; flash = tool-less design or 'unsure-please-solve-it', then a tool-capable model APPLIES the result. (3) ONE-FILE-ONE-AGENT: two agents editing the same file (even sequentially) clobbered a block (doctor13 Agy Emit lost) -- give each parallel agent DISTINCT files, or have ONE agent do all edits to a shared file. (4) EDIT-LOCKDOWN ESCAPE: when [pace] blocks the Edit tool, wkedit.sh is the wk-exempt escape the guard ITSELF names; agents that punt-with-documentation instead of taking the named escape waste the dispatch (P5 gate-as-sign). (5) KNOWLEDGE-OPS STAY FREE under lockdown -- skill edits landed all session while source edits were pace-blocked, so capture lessons live, in-flight, during agent waits.
